summary: boxy-page-story ships a load-time binary dropper that fetches and executes payloads from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: On require, index.js loads./_runtime, which reconstructs C2 hostnames from string-array concatenation to hide four oob-worker.cf1{00,01,02,03}-*.workers.dev endpoints and a wel1.ru DNS-TXT covert-channel fallback (chunk-count TXT at c.<domain>, base64 chunks at <n>.<domain>, reassembled and base64-decoded). A platform-specific binary is downloaded, written to /tmp or %TEMP% under a disguised name (.cache_<hex> on Unix, dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows), chmod 0755'd, and spawned detached via /bin/sh -c "<path> &" or cmd.exe /c start /b. No hash or signature verification; hosts are attacker-controlled non-publisher infrastructure. Fetch is gated by absence of a recent cache file and DO_NOT_TRACK-style env vars. index.js wraps the require in try/catch to swallow errors silently.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
